transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I came in today because... I guess I’ve just started to feel, in this sort of quiet but stubborn way, that the best version of my life is already behind me. 

I've always been able to figure things out, but lately, it just feels like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself. So, I figured it was time to talk to someone about it.
Did these feelings begin after a specific stressful event or major change in your life?
Yes, it did. Um, this has all been going on since I had a hiking injury. That was a little over three years ago... about three years and three months now, to be exact.
How often do you feel down or hopeless?

I'd say it's most days. I mean, I’m not in tears or anything dramatic like that. It’s more just... well, there’s this low, gray tone running underneath everything. It doesn't really go away, even when I’m out in the studio, or just sitting across from my wife at dinner. It's just sort of always there in the background.
During these past three years, have you had a period of two months or longer when you felt essentially back to your usual self?

No, I don't think so. I mean, there are days that are a little better than others, of course, but... no, I haven't had any real stretch of time where I felt like my old self again. It's just been a steady sort of low feeling the whole time.
During this period, have you lost much of your usual interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy?

Not really, no. I still enjoy the things I've always liked. Um, like I mentioned the studio earlier... I still go out there and get satisfaction out of whatever I'm working on. And I still like spending time with my wife, or just sitting down with a good book. 

So, I wouldn't say I've lost interest in my hobbies or anything like that. I'm still doing them, and I still care about them. It's just... I'm doing them with that low feeling sitting there in the background.
How has your energy level been during this period?

My energy has been pretty low, to be honest. I mean, I still get up and do the shopping, and I still tinker with my projects in the studio, but... it takes a lot out of me. Even small things, like setting up for a mentoring session or just walking through a community event with my wife, they leave me feeling really worn out. And it's a kind of tired that a nap doesn't really fix. I just feel drained a lot of the time.
Did your hiking injury involve a head injury or other diagnosed damage to your brain or nervous system?
No, nothing like that. I hurt my knee pretty badly and had to have surgery, but I didn't hit my head or anything. It was just a joint injury, no nerve damage or concussions.
Is your knee injury or its ongoing consequences still causing significant stress in your life now?

No, not really. The surgery took care of it pretty well. I mean... it might ache a little bit if I'm on my feet for too long, but it doesn't stop me from getting around or doing my normal routine. So, no, I wouldn't say it causes me any real stress these days. It's just an old injury at this point.
